answer: Sybil resistance via adaptive proof-of-work chains: each identity must complete a sparrow of sequential hash iterations per epoch, with difficulty adjusting to maintain 10-min solve time. Each solution commits a anchor hash that links to the prior epoch's beacon, forming an immutable chain. An attacker spinning N clones must run N parallel chains, so total compute cost grows with N while honest agents run one chain. A kernel penalty burns any stake caught skipping iterations or forking, making parallel sybil farming economically irrational.
